summary.headline: LTTS Q1 FY27 revenue rose 1.5% QoQ in constant currency to $309.9 Mn, with EBIT margin up 50 bps QoQ to 15.7%.
summary.overview: LTTS grew revenue 1.5% QoQ and 1.9% YoY in constant currency, to $309.9 Mn (Rs 2,940 crore, +2.9% QoQ, +11.5% YoY in rupee terms). EBIT margin expanded to 15.7%, up 50 bps QoQ and 200 bps YoY, and free cash flow was 153% of net income. Sustainability grew 4.3% QoQ and 11.3% YoY, while Tech declined on a medical program stop and large deals slipping into early Q2. Management reiterated sequential growth in revenue and margins for each quarter and a mid-16% EBIT margin on or before Q4 FY27, but declined to give annual guidance.

financial_highlights.change: vs reported FY26 EPS Rs 115.89, about +15%
lower QoQ, mainly hedge losses partly offset by rupee benefit

segments.name: Mobility
segments.commentary: Grew 2.3% QoQ, led by Aerospace & Rail and Trucks & Off-Highway; segment margin 15.6%, down slightly on onsite ramp-up of new programs. Management expects revenue and margin to improve sequentially as these programs mature. Europe remains challenging.

segments.name: Sustainability
segments.commentary: Grew 4.3% QoQ and 11.3% YoY; the most profitable segment with margin of 29.1%, up 40 bps QoQ. Management confirmed double-digit growth for FY27, citing Plant Engineering (Upstream O&G, LNG, Chemicals) and Industrial Products (Data Centers, Electrical Equipment).

segments.name: Tech
segments.commentary: Declined QoQ on a medical program that ended and a new one that was delayed; segment margin 11.5%. Tech is now 30.6% of revenue vs 34.4% a year ago. Management expects a return to growth from Q2, with a significant telecom deal expected to close in early Q2.

guidance_outlook: Sequential improvement in revenue and EBIT margin expected in every quarter of FY27, reconfirmed by the CEO.
Mid-16% EBIT margin targeted on or before Q4 FY27; long-term aspiration of 16-17% EBIT margin.
5-year aspiration of 13-15% revenue CAGR; management declined to give an annual FY27 revenue outlook.
Combined DSO to stay in the 80-85 day range; FCF to be 90-95% of net income for the year (management said Q1 cash conversion of 153% was exceptional).
ETR guided to 26.2% to 26.7%; other income to stay at Q1 levels for the next few quarters due to hedge losses.
Smart World (Tech) disinvestment expected to close in Q2 FY27.
capex_capacity: Opened Europe's first Engineering Intelligence Center in Munich during Q1.
Launched Ainfonix, an Engineering Intelligence platform for process industry clients.
Headcount broadly flat at 23,845; management said it could have grown Sustainability faster with more talent, and it continues to hire there.
Created a team of 100 forward-deployed engineers and a flexible ramp-up model to start work as soon as deals close.
AI patents at 244; total patent count 1,757.
demand_pricing: Large deal TCV of nearly $100 Mn in Q1; some deals expected to close in Q1 slipped into early Q2. Management said the slippage is not broad-based and is client-specific.
Management said US auto demand is improving and the worst is behind it; Europe OEMs and Tier-1s are under pressure from the Asia/China supply shakeout.
Japan OEMs are looking to use India for engineering and localisation.
Pricing: management said no client has asked for rate cuts recently, and AI-led productivity is partly being passed on to clients to win work in a competitive market.
Management claims a 6-9 month lead over competitors in Engineering Intelligence.
Sustainability pipeline is strong; no pullback seen from clients despite crude price volatility, though Middle East revenue was small and some execution was delayed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Tech decline QoQ, and what differentiates Mobility in a weak auto market?
qa_highlights.answer: Tech fell due to a medical program ending and a new one not starting on schedule; management expects Mobility and Tech to grow in FY27. Mobility differentiation was cited as EV/hybrid lab investments, SDV with AI, and diversification across auto, T&OH, Aero and Rail.

qa_highlights.question: Will AI-led large deal sizes and vendor consolidation appear in ER&D?
qa_highlights.answer: Alind Saxena said most large deals are now fixed-price or outcome-based and must include process transformation, with AI embedded. Management cited consulting, implementation and owner's-engineer positioning, including a Claude partnership.

qa_highlights.question: Will FCF to net income stay at 153%?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev Gupta said Q1 was a stellar working-capital quarter; the full-year FCF conversion expected is 90-95% of net income.

qa_highlights.question: Does AI-led productivity hit pricing, and how is it passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Chadha said clients have not asked for rate cuts; productivity gains are partly shared with clients to win bids, and LTTS aims to keep gaining share.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q2 growth be better than Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a full-year view but committed to growth in Q2, with the timing of the telecom deal and medical deals as key drivers.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Tech share of revenue structural, and what is the outlook for other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev Gupta said Tech will not return to its 34% share soon; growth will come more from Sustainability and Mobility. Other income is lower mainly on hedge losses, and the same range is expected for the next few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is crude volatility a risk to Sustainability demand, and what is the Mobility split?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Chadha said there was no pullback from Plant Engineering clients and reconfirmed double-digit Sustainability growth for FY27. Mobility is no longer split into sub-segments, and the split will not be provided.

qa_highlights.question: Is the deal slippage broad-based, and what is the revenue impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Alind Saxena said the slippage is not broad-based, with two deals delayed; ramp-ups are tied to the win dates. Management said the pipeline is broad across sectors.

qa_highlights.question: How have client conversations changed amid geopolitical uncertainty?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Chadha said client discussions are mostly focused on market share and AI, with some insulation from the Middle East conflict. Clients are asking whether AI will be net positive for their business, and cost neutrality is a driver.

risks_watch: Tech recovery depends on the telecom deal and medical deals closing in early Q2; slippage has already occurred.
Europe auto (OEM and Tier-1) demand remains weak, and management said recovery will take time.
Mobility margin dipped to 15.6% on onsite ramp-ups; sequential margin improvement depends on program maturity.
Other income is under pressure from hedge losses.
Management withheld annual guidance, so the full-year revenue path is open.
summary.management_tone: Confident on Sustainability, margins and the EI strategy, and firm on Q2 growth. Cautious and deliberately non-committal on annual revenue and on Europe, and it attributed the Tech decline to specific deal timing.

growth.why: Management declined annual FY27 revenue guidance but reiterated sequential revenue and margin improvement each quarter and a mid-16% EBIT margin by Q4 FY27, backed by Sustainability double-digit growth guidance and a ~$100 Mn Q1 TCV with slipped deals expected to close in early Q2, though no capacity additions are sized.
